title: get_gravity() returns wrong values after the position of the object changes
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.6.beta3.official [76dda5c6c], 4.5.stable.official and 4.5.1.stable.official, 4.4.stable.official and 4.4.1.stable.official. - Also reproducible in the version 4.3, but requires manually pointing files due to the problems understand the UID identifiers from 4.5. ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.6.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory ### Issue description After calling set_position(), get_gravity() returns wrong, highly exaggerated values through first two physics frames, inside the Area2D that serves as a gravity point. Instead, I would expect it to return proper values instantly, not requiring me to workaround the problem through these two frames. Here's the output of the fragment after the `star_entered_var = 4` variable is set after teleporting: ``` star_entered_var: 4 get_gravity: (-14.67699, -579.8051) delta: 0.01666666666667 velocity: (-0.244617, -9.663419) --- star_entered_var: 3 get_gravity: (-21.55693, -773.7246) delta: 0.01666666666667 velocity: (-0.603899, -22.55883) --- star_entered_var: 2 get_gravity: (-1.362697, -1.356538) delta: 0.01666666666667 velocity: (-0.62661, -22.58144) --- star_entered_var: 1 get_gravity: (-1.365729, -1.357605) delta: 0.01666666666667 velocity: (-0.649373, -22.60407) ``` Notice how values after the third and the fourth execution are much lower than in the first and second execution, which are much closer to the values I would expect for the function to return immediately. Here are the settings for the Area2D that serves as a gravity point: I also didn't forget about globally disabling the gravity: ### Steps to reproduce player.gd: ```gdscript class_name Player extends CharacterBody2D @export var acceleration = 100.0 var star_entered_var = 0 func _ready() -> void: pass func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"): velocity += Vector2.UP.rotated(rotation) * acceleration * delta if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"): rotate(-PI / 2 * delta) if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"): rotate(PI / 2 * delta) velocity += get_gravity() * delta if star_entered_var > 0: print("---") print("star_entered_var: " + str(star_entered_var)) print("get_gravity: " + str(get_gravity())) print("delta: " + str(delta)) print("velocity: " + str(velocity)) star_entered_var -= 1 move_and_slide() func _input(event): if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed: if event.keycode == KEY_Z: print("get_gravity" + str(get_gravity())) func star_entered(): print("Position: " + str(position)) set_position(Vector2(768,768)) velocity = Vector2.ZERO star_entered_var = 4 ``` star.gd: ```gdscript class_name Star extends Area2D # Called when the node enters the scene tree for the first time. func _ready() -> void: pass # Called every frame. 'delta' is the elapsed time since the previous frame. func _process(delta: float) -> void: pass func _on_kill_area_2d_body_entered(body: Node2D) -> void: if body is Player: body.star_entered() ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) This project is put in an Asteroids-like environment, except there's a star with a gravitional force (representing the gravity point) in the middle. Controls should be self-explanatory, you control the ship with the up arrow key for thrust, and rotate with the left and right arrow keys. [teleport-gravity-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24508867/teleport-gravity-bug.zip) In order to reproduce the bug, fly the ship into a star and when it respawns, take notice that it tends to go in the direction it was going before. The `print()` instructions are included in the code to demonstrate that the problem is caused by the faulty get_gravity() readouts. This is especially noticeable when the star was approached in a different direction (that is, when flown to from behind or besides the respawn point).
